column3: The Hebrew explicitly says Boaz “went up” to the gate and refers to the other man with an unnamed-person formula. BSB omits the upward direction and addresses him as “my friend.”
The Hebrew leaves the subject unnamed; BSB supplies Boaz. It explicitly repeats that they sat, where BSB uses “did so.”
The Hebrew says Naomi “has sold” the portion of the field; BSB has “is selling”.
The Hebrew uses the image “uncover your ear,” rendered “inform you” in BSB. The negative condition has third-person “he will not redeem,” whereas BSB addresses the man as “you will not redeem.”
The Hebrew describes buying the field “from the hand of Naomi”; BSB renders this as buying it “from Naomi.”
The Hebrew repeats the redemption root in the command “redeem for yourself my redemption”; BSB renders this as “Take my right of redemption.”
The Hebrew joins redemption and exchange with “and”; BSB uses “or” and explicitly supplies “of property.” It calls the recipient the man’s “companion,” where BSB has “the other party.”
The Hebrew places the speech before removing the sandal; BSB puts removing the sandal first.
The Hebrew says “I have acquired,” where BSB has “I am buying.” It repeats “all that belonged to” for the property of Chilion and Mahlon and uses the image “from Naomi’s hand.”
The Hebrew repeats “the name of the deceased,” where BSB uses “his name” on the second occurrence. It describes the name as not being “cut off,” rendered “disappear” in BSB.
The Hebrew’s final commands literally say to “do valor” and “call a name”; BSB renders them as wishes to be prosperous and famous.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says Boaz “went in to her” and that the LORD “gave her conception”; BSB uses “had relations with her” and “enabled her to conceive.”
The Hebrew wishes that his name “may be called in Israel”; BSB makes the renown explicit with “become famous.”
The Hebrew describes him as “a restorer of soul” and sustaining her “gray hair”; BSB uses the verbs “renew your life” and “sustain you in your old age.”
The child is placed at her bosom; BSB says “on her lap”.
The Hebrew first says the neighboring women called a name for him, then repeats that they called his name Obed. BSB combines this into a single naming statement.
The Hebrew actively says Perez “begot” Hezron; BSB expresses this as Perez “was the father of” Hezron.
The Hebrew actively uses “begot” for both generations; BSB uses “was the father of.”
